input.quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives us (Corio) and our Customers a full defend-and-indemnify from Commerce One for third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control, cooperation at Vendor's expense, right to join with own counsel) and the usual remedy ladder (procure rights, replace/modify, or terminate with pro-rated refund of fees paid). The Section 8.2 carve-outs are customary (use outside the Documentation; modification by a third party) and are no broader than the exclusions the fallback tolerates. There is no reciprocal Corio indemnity for the Vendor's software, so the walk-away scenario (one-way Customer indemnity) does not arise. Section 9 expressly excludes "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" from both the 12-month fee cap and the consequential-damages waiver, so the Vendor indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. The clause therefore satisfies the fallback and substantially reaches the preferred position on IP. Noted but not flagged: the indemnity does not extend to Vendor's breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to Corio data, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, which are preferred-position add-ons rather than material failures of the fallback.
